paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: This grouped bar chart illustrates the negative log probabilities for a baseline language model and several fine-tuned models evaluated across different clinical specialty terms. The horizontal axis contains the categories, labeled "Per-specialty terms," and displays six groups arranged in the following order: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical value axis is labeled "Negative log probability" and features a linear scale ranging from -27 at the bottom to -22 at the top, with numeric tick marks spaced at intervals of 1 unit. As a result of this negative scale, the bars extend downward from the -22 baseline toward more negative values. Within each of the six categories along the horizontal axis, there is a group of seven adjacent, vertically oriented bars. According to the top unboxed legends, the first bar in each group, colored light blue, represents the "MistralV0.2-Base" model. The subsequent six bars in each group represent models "Fine-tuned on:" the six clinical specialties, identified by a sequential color gradient ranging from light beige (Cardio) through progressively darker shades of tan and brown (Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics) to dark brown (Pediatrics). Visually, the light blue baseline bar consistently extends the furthest downward (to the most negative value) within every group, reaching an approximate chart maximum extension of -26.7 in the Cardio category and its shortest extension of roughly -23.8 in the Infect category. The six fine-tuned bars in each group are consistently shorter than the baseline bar; for example, the fine-tuned bars in the Cardio group terminate between approximately -25.7 and -26.1, while the fine-tuned bars in the Infect group are visually the shortest in the chart, trailing off between approximately -22.9 and -23.2. The bars within each grouping strictly follow the categorical order defined in the legend rather than being sorted by value, and there is no supplementary visual emphasis such as bolding, outlining, or individual numeric annotation on the chart.
